                                            INTRODUCTION
8
            1.      Plaintiffs bring this class action to address Defendant’s outrageous, illegal, and
9
     widespread practice of disclosing—without consent—the Nonpublic Personal Information 1 and
10

11
     Personally Identifiable Financial Information 2 (together, “Personal and Financial Information”) of

12   Plaintiffs and the proposed Class Members to third parties, including Meta Platforms, Inc. d/b/a

13   Meta (“Facebook” or “Meta”), Google, LLC (“Google”), Microsoft Corp. (“Microsoft”), Tavant,
14
     LogRocket, and possibly others (collectively the “Third Parties”) (in short, “the Disclosure”).
15
            2.      Lakeview is a massive mortgage lender and servicer that provides services to
16

17

18   operates and encourages its customers to use its website, https://www.lakeview.com/ (the

19   “Website”), on which customers can, among other things, access their account information, obtain
20
     information about Lakeview’s services, and apply for financing and refinancing.

            1
                The United States Congress defines “nonpublic personal information” as “personally
23
     identifiable financial information-- (i) provided by a consumer to a financial institution; (ii)
24   resulting from any transaction with the consumer or any service performed for the consumer; or
     (iii) otherwise obtained by the financial institution.” The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C.A.
25   § 6809(4)(A) (“GLBA”).
              2
                “Personally identifiable financial information means any information: (i) A consumer
26
     provides to [a financial institution] to obtain a financial product or service from [the financial
27   institution]; (ii) About a consumer resulting from any transaction involving a financial product or
     service between [a financial institution] and a consumer; or (iii) [a financial institution]
28   otherwise obtain[s] about a consumer in connection with providing a financial product or service
     to that consumer.” 16 C.F.R. § 313.3(o)(1).

            3.      Despite its unique position as a massive and trusted mortgage lender and servicer,

4

5    provision of mortgage services—entirely without their knowledge or authorization. Lakeview did

6    so by knowingly and secretly configuring and implementing code-based tracking devices
7
     (“trackers” or “tracking technologies”) into its Website.
8

9
     Financial Information that Customers input into and accessed on Lakeview’s Website. This
10

11   information includes without limitation, the kind of loans Customers are seeking; their status as a

12   Customer; when they create new accounts; their browsing activities, including that the user clicked
13
     certain buttons and what URLs or webpages they led to; and that a Customer is filling out an
14
     application.
15

16

17   to save costs on its marketing campaigns, improve its data analytics, attract new customers, and

18   generate sales. Lakeview benefited from use of Customers’ Personal and Financial Information.
19
     Lakeview further allowed the Third Parties, who are uninvolved in Lakeview’s provision of
20
     mortgage services, to profit from its Disclosure of Customers’ Private and Financial information.
21
     And the Third Parties used Customers’ Personal and Financial Information for themselves and

25   product or service . . . that is to be used primarily for personal, family, or household purposes, or
     that individual’s legal representative.” 16 C.F.R. § 313.3; 15 U.S.C.A. § 6809(9).
26            4
                “Customer means a consumer who has a customer relationship with [a financial
27   institution].” 16 C.F.R. § 313.3. “The term ‘time of establishing a customer relationship’ shall . .
     . in the case of a financial institution engaged in extending credit directly to consumers to finance
28   purchases of goods or services, mean the time of establishing the credit relationship with the
     consumer.” 15 U.S.C.A. § 6809.

26

27

     example, failing to provide Customers with appropriate notice that their information was being
